title: Machine images with Packer, and immutable, reproducible infrastructure

videos.script: Every machine in the shop starts from an image. The question is when the software gets onto it. {{boot}} One answer is at boot. Each new machine installs nginx as it comes up, from whatever the archive offers that day. Three machines started on three different days can run three different versions. {{bake}} The other answer is to bake. You build the image once, with everything installed, and start every machine as a copy of it. {{packer}} Packer does the building. A template names a base image, the steps to run inside it, and what to call the result. Here it builds a real Docker image on the laptop, and you run it to see whether it works. {{version}} Every build gets a version that is never reused, so a name always means the same contents. {{terraform}} Then Terraform rolls it out. A new version is a one-line change, and the plan replaces the machine instead of editing it. Rolling back is the same change, with the older number. {{pin}} Last, you pin every input, so the same template builds the same software next month. That is the immutable infrastructure of lesson one, finally in commands.
